notes.summary: GJKM 1712.00980v3 supplies equal-characteristic-p envelope and model replacements under geometric-origin and resolution hypotheses; surfaces over curve-function-field completions are unconditional. Its stated equation theorem retains SNC-skeleton support and does not cover mixed characteristic.
notes.detailedSummary: The exact PDF requires a complete nontrivially discretely valued characteristic-p field and geometric origin over a perfect characteristic-p field. Envelope continuity requires resolution in total dimension d+n; the transferred SNC-based pluripotential theory additionally requires embedded resolution. GJKM Theorem 6.3 states both resolution inputs in dimension three, making n=2,d=1 unconditional. Section 9 explicitly transfers BFJ bounded operators, locality, comparison, and energy theory, including the finite-energy construction in section 6. Theorem 9.3 itself still assumes skeleton-supported measures. The supplied BFJ equation PDF is v1 with algebraizability and support restrictions; the Boucksom–Jonsson positive-characteristic surface endpoint is trivially valued.
notes.text:
This is a primary-source scope audit, not a complete solution of P16.3.

Gubler–Jell–Künnemann–Martin, with appendix authors Burgos Gil and Sombra, arXiv:1712.00980v3, is the exact supplied PDF. Its SHA256 is 6c506c3ee23c6e36900a59f3f3fba1f26c4b22708756324f89af8668ed5771b6. Starting in section 7, K is complete discretely valued and char(K)=p>0. Thus the higher-dimensional test-ideal results concern equal characteristic, not char(K)=0 with residue characteristic p.

Definition 8.1 requires a normal d-dimensional variety B over k, a codimension-one point b, K° identified with the completion of R=O_{B,b}, and a projective k(B)-variety whose base change is X. The field k must be perfect. This does not generally imply perfectness of K's residue field when d>1.

Theorem 8.2 assumes X smooth projective of dimension n and resolution over k in dimension d+n. It proves continuous envelopes, uniformly approximable by psh model functions, for every closed (1,1)-form with ample de Rham class. The chosen ample class need not descend to the initially chosen k(B)-variety; the published proof handles this at the model-envelope level.

Section 9 additionally assumes embedded resolution in dimension d+n. Definitions 6.1 and 6.2 specify projective regular resolutions, preserving the regular locus, and projective embedded resolutions between regular varieties, preserving the complement of the prescribed subset. Proposition 5.2 and section 9 use these to obtain cofinal projective SNC models, preserving the original smooth generic fiber. Theorem 6.3 states both resolution results in dimension three over perfect fields, citing Cossart–Piltant. Consequently n=2,d=1 is unconditional in this source. The separately cited Cossart–Piltant papers were not independently inspected.

Section 9 explicitly transfers BFJ singular-metric sections 1–7 and equation-paper sections 3–6. These provide compactness, the bounded operator, locality, energy, the nonpluripolar E1 operator, full mass, and comparison. Corollary 9.1 supplies decreasing model regularization, and Theorem 9.2 supplies orthogonality. Theorem 9.3, however, states existence and uniqueness only for positive Radon measures supported on a projective SNC skeleton, with raw mass equal to the polarization degree.

The test-ideal replacement uses subadditivity and uniform generation. PDF page 15 was visually checked: body Theorem 4.6 requires E−λD nef. The differently ordered displayed condition in introductory Theorem 1.3 is not used. In Theorem 7.3 the application E=mD, λ=m makes this difference zero. The smooth spread-out variety has dimension d+n, which controls the global-generation threshold.

Version checks matter. The supplied 1201.0188 PDF is actual v1, with residue characteristic zero, algebraizability, and SNC-dual-complex support in Theorem A. Its sequence regularization is Proposition 4.5, whereas GJKM cites later numbering. The supplied 1201.0187 is v2, whose compactness theorem is Theorem 7.10. ArXiv:1805.01016v3 is Boucksom–Eriksson's Spaces of norms, determinant of cohomology and Fekete points in non-Archimedean geometry. ArXiv:1801.08229v4 is a trivial-valuation theory; its positive-characteristic surface Theorem 12.9 cannot simply be applied to K=k((t)). ArXiv:2307.01697v1 studies finite-energy measures and model/test potentials; completion of measures alone does not establish E1 surjectivity.

Literal statements and proof passages, exact versions, hashes, and application checks are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Rerun: python3 audit_sources.py. All eleven supplied source hashes were verified, and 33 literal extracts were retained. This audit is confined to the supplied sources and is not an exhaustive contemporary literature survey.

notes.summary: Draft proof of genuine E1 existence and uniqueness for arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy measures on general smooth projective surfaces of geometric origin in nontrivially valued equal characteristic p. This narrower theorem remains partial for original P16.3.
notes.detailedSummary: Let K be the completion at a closed point of a normal curve's function field over a perfect characteristic-p field, and let X be the base change of a smooth geometrically integral projective surface. For any ample L, the genuine nonpluripolar E1 operator has raw mass V=(L²). Every positive Radon measure μ of mass V satisfying sup_v(E(v)−∫v dμ)<∞ has an E1 solution, unique modulo constants, without support or invariance restrictions. The new passage extends synthetic uniform integration estimates to energy-bounded E1 sets, proving actual variational attainment using GJKM compactness and differentiation. Uniqueness includes an explicit characteristic-independent vertical intersection kernel argument. This is a deduction from published inputs, not a claim of publication priority. Higher-dimensional geometric-origin cases retain both explicit resolution premises; mixed characteristic and unrestricted geometry remain outside the theorem.
notes.text:
The following is an unverified mathematical proof draft, with a concrete unconditional surface range. It does not claim the entire original P16.3.

THEOREM. Let k be perfect of characteristic p>0, B a normal integral curve over k, b a closed point, F=k(B), and K the completion of F at b with a nontrivial discrete absolute value. Let Y/F be a smooth geometrically integral projective surface and X=Y×F K. For any ample line bundle L on X, choose a semipositive model reference metric with curvature θ and put V=(L²)>0. There is an approximation-independent genuine mixed Monge–Ampère operator on E1(X,θ), of raw mass V. Every positive Radon measure μ on Xᵃⁿ with μ(Xᵃⁿ)=V and finite dual energy specified below admits an E1 solution, unique modulo additive constants. No skeleton support, torus invariance, or continuity of the solution is assumed.

Published geometric inputs are exactly those audited in n1. Here d+n=1+2=3, so GJKM Theorem 6.3 supplies both resolution inputs without an unproved premise. Its section 9 gives cofinal SNC models and transfers BFJ compactness and bounded/finite-energy calculus. Theorem 8.2 applies to any ample θ on this X, even when L does not descend to the original F-variety. Theorem 9.2 replaces the characteristic-zero orthogonality argument. No unbounded base-change or alteration descent is introduced.

A reference metric exists: embed X using a sufficiently high power of L, take its projective closure over K°, and pull O(1) to a dominating SNC model. Pullback preserves nefness by the curve projection formula, although it need not preserve ampleness. Taking the metric's root retains the original L and generic degree V.

1. Genuine operator and energy. The transferred BFJ Theorem 3.1 defines the bounded mixed operator by model intersections and decreasing approximation, with raw mass V and approximation independence. For bounded u set
E(u)=(1/(n+1))Σ[j=0,…,n]∫u(θ+ddᶜu)^j∧θ^(n−j), and e(u)=E(u)/V.
Extend e to psh u by the infimum over dominating psh model potentials. Transferred BFJ Proposition 6.2 gives concavity, monotonicity, weak upper semicontinuity, decreasing continuity, and e(u+c)=e(u)+c. Define E1={u psh:e(u)>−∞}.

For u≤0 set u_t=max(u,−t). Define the raw operator by
MAθ(u)=lim[t→∞] 1_{u>−t} MAθ(u_t), and m(u)=MAθ(u)/V.
Bounded locality makes these restricted measures increasing and compatible. Their limit is Radon. A constant shift only changes truncation thresholds, so it does not change the operator.

Full mass is proved, rather than assumed. The bounded energy difference formula gives
t·m(u_t){u≤−t}≤2(n+1)(e(u_{t/2})−e(u_t))→0.
Indeed u_{t/2}−u_t=t/2 on that set, and its integral against m(u_t), divided by n+1, is a nonnegative term of the energy difference. Decreasing continuity proves the limit. Thus MAθ(u) has exactly mass V and no pluripolar mass. The BFJ tail estimate
|∫f m(u_t)−∫f m(u)|≤2(n+1)|e(u)|·||f||∞/t
and bounded monotone continuity prove convergence along every decreasing E1 approximation. This establishes independence of model approximation as well as truncation.

Mixed E1 measures are obtained by simultaneous decreasing approximation and polarization: diagonal measures of all convex combinations converge, and finitely many diagonal values determine the mixed coefficients. The coefficients are limits of positive bounded mixed measures of mass V, hence positive, of mass V, and independent of choices. BFJ Lemma 6.10 and the positive expansion of the operator of a convex average give mixed E1 integrability.

Locality and comparison extend to E1:
1_{u>v}m(max(u,v))=1_{u>v}m(u), and ∫_{u<v}m(v)≤∫_{u<v}m(u).
Apply bounded locality on {u_t>v_t}, where the relevant nonpluripolar measures agree with their truncations, and let t increase. Discarded pole sets have zero mass. Full mass then turns locality of max into comparison. This is the characteristic-independent proof of transferred BFJ Proposition 6.11.

Transferred BFJ Proposition 6.12 gives de((1−t)u+tv)/dt at 0+=∫(v−u)m(u). With GJKM orthogonality, BFJ Theorem 7.2 and Corollary 7.3 also give the stronger two-sided envelope derivative
de(Pθ(u+tf))/dt at 0=∫f m(u)
for u∈E1 and continuous f. The hypotheses are checked: Pθ(u+tf) lies between u−|t|||f||∞ and u+|t|||f||∞, hence in E1; decreasing model u_j give decreasing envelopes converging to Pθ(u+tf). Decreasing energy/operator continuity and dominated convergence in the integrated continuous-envelope derivative extend the identity to u. Characteristic-zero multiplier ideals and BFJ's original orthogonality appendix are not used.

2. Exact measure condition. Put ν=μ/V, dividing the entire measure, never a restriction. Let Dθ denote psh tests in the real span of model functions. Require
E*θ(μ)=sup[v∈Dθ](E(v)−∫v dμ)<∞.
Equivalently A=e*(ν)=sup[v∈Dθ](e(v)−∫v dν)<∞, with E*θ(μ)=VA. Constants cancel because the raw mass is V. Rational model tests give the same supremum: on a common sufficiently high model, perturb a real nef class toward an ample representative of the same generic class, approximate vertical coefficients rationally inside the ample cone, and let the perturbation tend to zero. GJKM transfers the BFJ positivity input furnishing that representative.

For u∈E1 take decreasing model v_j→u. The bound ∫v_j dν≥e(v_j)−A≥e(u)−A, together with a uniform upper bound, proves u∈L1(ν) by monotone convergence. Moreover e(u)−∫u dν≤A. Thus this is also the supremum over all E1 potentials. Conversely mixed integrability and concavity give e(v)≤e(u)+∫(v−u)m(u), so e*(m(u))=e(u)−∫u m(u)<∞. The image and target therefore have the actual finite-energy meaning.

3. Synthetic application. Apply Boucksom–Jonsson arXiv:2307.01697v1 on the actual compact Berkovich space, with D the real span of model functions, Z the model numerical forms, and the usual intersection measures. D is dense, contains constants, and ddᶜ kills constants. Integration by parts is the model intersection identity. Seminegativity follows on a common regular SNC model from the vertical intersection formula in step 6 below, using arbitrary mixed nef classes in place of the ample product; its off-diagonal weights are nonnegative. Nef classes span Z, and on every finite-dimensional space their cone is closed by the nonnegative curve-degree inequalities. This checks the source's nice-order requirement. BFJ positivity, transferred by GJKM, verifies that θ has positive ample class; the n-linear pairing is nonzero since its volume is V.

The source's Definition 2.15 orthogonality also needs checking. Tests below f admit maxima through rational model maxima and uniform approximation with a strict constant margin. Their increasing directed net has supremum Pθ(f), continuous by GJKM. Dini convergence is uniform, so uniform operator continuity and GJKM Theorem 9.2 give
lim[v<f]∫(f−v)m(v)=∫(f−Pθf)m(Pθf)=0.
Thus the synthetic theorem is applicable, without assuming completeness of unbounded potentials.

Write m₀=m(0), J(u,v)=e(u)−e(v)+∫(v−u)m(u), J(u)=∫u m₀−e(u), and aν(v)=A−e(v)+∫v dν. For tests, synthetic Theorem 1.33 and Proposition 2.2 give quasi-symmetry and
J(u,v)≤C_n(aν(u)+aν(v)), and J(v)≤C_n(A+aν(v)).
The first bound follows directly from uniform concavity at the midpoint: the linear target terms cancel. The second uses u=0.

Theorem 2.23 and Lemma 2.25 give maximizing tests r_j with aν(r_j)→0 and bounded J(r_j), and equation (2.27), with the other potential zero, yields
|∫v(ν−m(r_j))|≤C_{n,R} aν(r_j)^(1/2)
whenever J(v), J(r_j), and A have a common fixed bound. Only this model-level uniform integration estimate is used. Completion of measures is not used to infer surjectivity.

4. New integration passage. Normalized PSH is compact in the topology of uniform convergence on each SNC dual complex. Integration against m₀ is continuous, since this measure has finite divisorial support. Hence −T≤∫u m₀≤0 for sup u=0 and a fixed finite T.

The sets K_C={u psh:sup u=0,e(u)≥−C} are compact by upper semicontinuity of e, and satisfy 0≤J(u)≤C. For u∈K_C choose decreasing model u_l→u. Both energy and its m₀ integral converge, so J(u_l) is eventually bounded by C+1. The integrability already proved permits monotone passage in the ν integral; m(r_j) also integrates u, since it has finite divisorial support. Passing l→∞ in the test estimate therefore gives
sup[u∈K_C]|∫u dν−∫u m(r_j)|≤C_{n,R}aν(r_j)^(1/2)→0.
Each functional ∫u m(r_j) is weakly continuous. Their uniform limit proves continuity of ∫u dν on K_C. This is the indispensable potential-space argument replacing skeleton support.

5. Actual existence. Normalize maximizing tests v_i by sup v_i=0. Their J are bounded by the defect estimate, and −e(v_i)=J(v_i)−∫v_i m₀≤J(v_i)+T. They therefore lie eventually in one compact K_C. Take a weakly convergent subnet to u∈K_C, without assuming sequential compactness. Integral continuity and upper semicontinuity of energy yield e(u)−∫u dν≥limsup(e(v_i)−∫v_i dν)=A. The dual-energy bound gives equality.

For continuous f put u_t=Pθ(u+tf) and h(t)=e(u_t)−∫(u+tf)dν. Positivity and maximality imply h(t)≤e(u_t)−∫u_t dν≤A=h(0). The two-sided envelope derivative gives 0=h′(0)=∫f m(u)−∫f dν. Equality against all continuous tests proves m(u)=ν, hence raw MAθ(u)=μ. The actual E1 potential is constructed by variational attainment, not by defining an inverse measure.

6. Uniqueness, including the strict kernel. Suppose m(u)=m(v), and set f=u−v. All following terms are finite by mixed E1 integrability. Model reference changes η=θ+ddᶜg are legitimate: bounded/model operators coincide after replacing u by u−g, and decreasing continuity proves this in E1. The energy cocycle eη(u−g)=eθ(u)−eθ(g) proves finite energy after reference change.

For a surface set η_u=η+ddᶜ(u−g), η_v=η+ddᶜ(v−g), and N_T(f)=−∫f ddᶜf∧T. Integration by parts gives N_{η_u}(f)+N_{η_v}(f)=V∫f(m(v)−m(u))=0. Each term is nonnegative. Cauchy–Schwarz with f and u−g therefore gives ∫f ddᶜ(u−g)∧η_u=∫f ddᶜ(u−g)∧η_v=0. Subtracting, and using ddᶜf=η_u−η_v, proves ∫f ddᶜf∧ddᶜ(u−g)=0. Thus N_η(f)=0.

Choose a sufficiently high regular SNC model with a relatively ample rational representative A of the original generic ample class, obtained using the transferred BFJ positivity input. Write the special fiber as Σb_iE_i. For i≠j put w_ij=(E_i·E_j·A^(n−1)); these are nonnegative and strictly positive when the components meet. The principal-fiber relation eliminates diagonal terms and gives, for D=Σa_iE_i,
D²·A^(n−1)=−Σ[i<j]b_i b_j w_ij(a_i/b_i−a_j/b_j)².
The intersection graph is connected: normal proper models with geometrically integral generic fiber have global functions K°, by integrality and integrally closedness; Stein factorization gives connected fibers. Hence equality forces a_i/b_i constant across components, in every residue characteristic.

Let λ=−log|π| and a_i=b_i f(x_i)/λ at component divisorial points. The model function g_D equals f at these vertices. Cauchy–Schwarz and N_η(f)=0 give ∫f ddᶜg_D∧η^(n−1)=0, which the model intersection formula identifies with λD²·A^(n−1). Thus f has one value on all those vertices. Keep a fixed divisorial anchor while refining models; cofinality places every other divisorial point together with the anchor on a dominating model. The constants consequently agree. Psh determination by divisorial values gives u=v+c everywhere. Normalizing both suprema to zero gives c=0.

The same existence argument works for geometric-origin n-folds under BOTH resolution premises in dimension d+n. The higher-dimensional zero-norm estimate is the characteristic-independent repeated Cauchy–Schwarz proof of BFJ Proposition 8.2, with the same transferred mixed calculus; the strict kernel above applies unchanged. That range remains conditional when the resolution premises are unproved.

The complete argument and exact application checks are in P16.3-argument.md and the standalone P16.3-paper.tex. These are deductions from the sources, not a claim of literature priority or execution-verified mathematics. Mixed characteristic, unrestricted higher dimension, and removal of geometric origin remain original obligations.
